security_audit.summary: The skill documents useful multi-agent coordination workflows, but several examples ask users to run unpinned external CLI commands. I found no prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent, but setup, update, dashboard, and bridge commands require explicit approval and safer pinning.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the oh-my-ag package version, document the trusted source, and require user approval before installer or update commands run.
State that dashboard and SSE bridge services must bind only to localhost and must not expose project data without authentication.
Add approval gates before Bash commands write to .agent or .serena directories, especially during setup and repair workflows.

remediation.issue: Executable examples mixed with reference text
remediation.suggestion: Mark risky commands as manual steps and separate them from passive configuration examples.

content.value_statement: Complex projects need clear handoffs between planning, implementation, QA, and debugging agents. This skill defines a Serena Memory based workflow for coordinating specialized agents and monitoring progress.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use PM, frontend, backend, debug, and workflow guide agents.
Defines Serena Memory as the shared state location for agent coordination.
Lists setup, doctor, dashboard, bridge, update, and usage commands.
Shows how to spawn a backend agent for a specific task.
Documents per-agent CLI mapping for Gemini, Codex, and Claude.
Describes terminal and web dashboards for workflow monitoring.
limitations: Requires external oh-my-ag, Bun, and uv tooling before workflows can run.
Does not include implementation code for agents, dashboards, or Serena itself.
Commands are examples and may change with the upstream package.
Network bridge and dashboard setup need local security review.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Full Stack Delivery
use_cases.description: Assign planning, frontend, backend, QA, and debugging work across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Set Up Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Install the oh-my-ag workflow and verify local tools before starting coordinated work.

use_cases.title: Monitor Multi-Agent Sessions
use_cases.description: Use Serena Memory and dashboards to follow status across active agent tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Start Coordination
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ohmg to coordinate this project: [goal]. Identify the agents needed and the first shared state entries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Agent Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Break down [feature] into PM, frontend, backend, QA, and debug responsibilities using the ohmg workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Configure CLI Mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a per-agent CLI mapping for a project that uses Codex for backend, Claude for QA, and Gemini for frontend.

prompt_templates.title: Run Observability Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my multi-agent session plan. Include Serena Memory checkpoints, dashboard monitoring, bridge needs, and security concerns.

output_examples.output: Agent plan with PM requirements, backend API work, frontend form tasks, QA checks, and shared Serena Memory checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Verify my ohmg setup before a sprint.
output_examples.output: Checklist covering Bun, uv, oh-my-ag doctor, agent skill installation, CLI mapping, and dashboard readiness.
Triage summary showing current agent status, missing handoffs, next owner, and suggested dashboard checks.

best_practices: Review every shell command before execution, especially installer, update, bridge, and dashboard commands.
Keep Serena Memory entries structured so agents can resume work without guessing.
Map each agent to a CLI that matches the task and your account limits.
anti_patterns: Do not run unpinned package commands in sensitive repositories without approval.
Do not spawn agents before defining shared goals, owners, and completion criteria.
Do not expose bridges or dashboards outside localhost without authentication.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate specialized AI agents for planning, frontend, backend, QA, debugging, and monitoring work.

faq.question: Does it install agents by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands that can install or update the oh-my-ag workflow when a user approves them.

faq.question: Which tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions Gemini, Claude, Codex, Claude Code, Bun, uv, Serena Memory, and Google Antigravity.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Some documented commands may fetch packages or open local dashboard and bridge endpoints.

faq.question: Can I use it for a single small task?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is most useful when work spans several domains or agents.

faq.question: What should I review before use?
faq.answer: Review package commands, local bridge URLs, dashboard access, and changes written under agent or Serena directories.
